description: Server-side scheduled sync that guarantees EVERY Gmail thread tagged with a '<Name> lead' label becomes a lead assigned to that salesperson, across the FULL mailbox, independent of who is logged in or which tab is open. This is the core fix. It has three coordinated parts: (a) a new Apps Script action that enumerates all label-tagged threads via Gmail search (not just inbox page 1); (b) a new gmail-bridge proxy action to reach it; (c) a new `gmail-tag-sync` Supabase edge function driven by pg_cron that reads tagged threads, parses real customer fields, matches the owner tag to a profile, dedups, and inserts leads via the service-role client. Mirrors the existing process-reminders / notify-stale-followups cron pattern.
steps: APPS SCRIPT (setup/gmail-apps-script.gs): Add a new doGet action `action=tagged` that uses GmailApp.search('label:\"lead\" OR ...') — more robustly, iterate GmailApp.getUserLabels(), keep only labels whose name matches /\blead$/i, and for each use label.getThreads(start, max) (or GmailApp.search with pagination) to collect threads. For each thread return { threadId, from (first message From), subject, date, unread, labels[], url } exactly like the inbox action, PLUS optionally the first message plain body under `body` (guarded in try/catch, truncated to a few KB) so the sync can parse customer fields without a second round-trip. Support `start` and `max` (cap max at 100) for pagination and return `hasMore`. Reuse the existing token check and JSON response shape. Keep the existing inbox/thread/claim actions unchanged. Add a short header comment documenting the new action. NOTE in the file and in findings that the LIVE Apps Script is deployed externally and the owner must paste + redeploy this file for the change to take effect.

GMAIL-BRIDGE (supabase/functions/gmail-bridge/index.ts): Add an `action === 'tagged'` branch that GETs `${WEBHOOK_URL}?action=tagged&max=..&start=..&token=..` and returns { ok, emails, hasMore, start } exactly like the inbox branch. Cap max at 100, clamp start >= 0. Keep all existing branches intact. Update the top-of-file comment block to list the new action.

SHARED PARSING FOR DENO: The server function cannot import the browser module src/lib/gmail.ts. Create a Deno-compatible helper module supabase/functions/_shared/gmail-parse.ts that re-implements (copied, kept in sync with the JSDoc note added in FEAT-001) the pure functions needed server-side: parseFrom, claimedOwner, normalizeOwnerTag, isThrowawayAddress, htmlToText, parseWeb3FormLead, and matchOwnerTagToName. These must be behavior-identical to src/lib/gmail.ts. Add a comment cross-referencing src/lib/gmail.ts as the source of truth.

EDGE FUNCTION (supabase/functions/gmail-tag-sync/index.ts): New Deno.serve function following process-reminders exactly for scaffolding: corsHeaders, json() helper, CRON_SECRET auth accepting body.secret OR x-cron-secret header (401 on mismatch), createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY,{auth:{persistSession:false}}). Steps inside: (1) Page through the gmail-bridge `tagged` action by calling the Apps Script directly via GMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL + GMAIL_TOKEN (this function has those secrets) OR by invoking gmail-bridge — prefer calling the Apps Script directly to avoid an extra hop and JWT concerns; read GMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL and GMAIL_TOKEN from Deno.env. Loop start=0,25,... until hasMore is false or a safety cap (e.g. 20 pages) is hit. (2) Load all profiles (id, full_name) via service-role client. (3) Load existing email-sourced leads (id, email, assigned_to) where source='email' and build a Set/Map of existing dedup keys (email lowercased). (4) For each tagged thread: extract owner via claimedOwner(labels); if none, skip. Match owner to a profile via matchOwnerTagToName(owner, profileNames); if NO match, collect it into an `unmatched` list (owner tag + threadId + subject) and DO NOT silently drop — include unmatched in the response summary and, best-effort, insert a row into a lightweight log (email_log with source='gmail-tag-sync', status='unmatched', subject) so admins can see it. (5) Parse real fields: prefer the thread `body` returned by the tagged action; if absent, fetch the thread via the Apps Script thread action. Run parseWeb3FormLead on the body; compute realEmail and senderAddr; build dedupKeys=[realEmail, senderAddr] lowercased/trimmed — the SAME rule as the client. (6) If any dedup key already exists in the leads map, skip (no duplicate). (7) Build the insert row: client_name (parsed name/email/subject fallback, never null), mobile (parsed phone or '' to satisfy NOT NULL), email (realEmail or null), city, company_name, source='email', notes (subject + gmail url + parsed extras), assigned_to = matched profile id, created_by = matched profile id. Insert in batches. Add newly-created keys to the in-memory map so the same run doesn't double-insert. (8) Return { ok:true, scanned, created, skipped_existing, unmatched: [...] }. Fail-soft with 200 + {ok:false,error} on unexpected errors, matching the repo pattern.

CONFIG (supabase/config.toml): Add a [functions.gmail-tag-sync] block. Since the cron authenticates with CRON_SECRET in the body (not a user JWT), set verify_jwt = false to match how process-reminders/notify-stale-followups are invoked by pg_cron. Confirm by reading config.toml how the other cron functions are declared and mirror exactly (if they rely on the default, match that; the reminders/stale-followup cron SQL sends only the anon key + secret, so verify_jwt=false is appropriate).

CRON SQL (setup/ADD_GMAIL_TAG_SYNC_CRON.sql): New file mirroring setup/ADD_STALE_FOLLOWUP_CRON.sql. Schedule the gmail-tag-sync function on a sensible cadence (e.g. every 10 minutes: '*/10 * * * *') via cron.schedule + net.http_post to https://<PROJECT_REF>.supabase.co/functions/v1/gmail-tag-sync with Authorization Bearer <ANON_KEY> and body jsonb_build_object('secret','<CRON_SECRET>'). Include the unschedule-if-exists guard and the verify/checks comments exactly in the style of the existing cron SQL files. Use the same <PROJECT_REF>/<ANON_KEY>/<CRON_SECRET> placeholder convention.

DOCS (setup/GMAIL_TAG_SYNC_SETUP.md): New doc explaining: what the function does (auto-creates a lead for every tagged Gmail thread, full mailbox, no admin/tab dependency), the required secrets (GMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL, GMAIL_TOKEN, CRON_SECRET — note SUPABASE_URL/SERVICE_ROLE are auto-injected), the deploy steps (paste updated setup/gmail-apps-script.gs and REDEPLOY the Web App; `supabase functions deploy gmail-tag-sync`; run setup/ADD_GMAIL_TAG_SYNC_CRON.sql with placeholders filled), and how unmatched owner tags are surfaced (response `unmatched` list + email_log rows). Mirror the tone/structure of setup/GMAIL_INBOX_SETUP.md.

supabase/functions/gmail-bridge/index.ts has a `tagged` action returning {ok,emails,hasMore,start}; all existing actions unchanged.

supabase/functions/_shared/gmail-parse.ts exists with Deno-compatible copies of parseFrom, claimedOwner, normalizeOwnerTag, isThrowawayAddress, htmlToText, parseWeb3FormLead, matchOwnerTagToName that are behavior-identical to src/lib/gmail.ts.

supabase/functions/gmail-tag-sync/index.ts exists, authenticates via CRON_SECRET (body.secret or x-cron-secret), uses the service-role client, pages the full tagged set, dedups on [realEmail, senderAddr] lowercased identical to the client, inserts leads assigned to the matched owner with source='email' and non-null client_name/mobile, and returns { scanned, created, skipped_existing, unmatched }.
Unmatched owner tags are NOT silently dropped: they appear in the response `unmatched` array and a best-effort email_log row (source='gmail-tag-sync', status='unmatched').

No duplicate lead is created for a thread whose customer email or relay sender already exists as an email-sourced lead.

Read the paging loop and confirm it iterates until hasMore is false or the safety cap, so the whole mailbox is covered (not one page).
Diff supabase/functions/_shared/gmail-parse.ts against src/lib/gmail.ts function-by-function and confirm identical logic (regexes, alias tables, fallbacks).
Read setup/ADD_GMAIL_TAG_SYNC_CRON.sql and confirm it matches the structure of setup/ADD_STALE_FOLLOWUP_CRON.sql (unschedule guard, net.http_post, placeholders).
Confirm gmail-bridge and Apps Script inbox/thread/claim branches are byte-for-byte unchanged except for the added tagged branch/action.

review_fixes_2026-09-03: Addressed review issues #1, #2, #3, #4, #5(server half). ISSUE #1 (500-thread run cap): raised the per-run sweep in supabase/functions/gmail-tag-sync/index.ts from MAX_PAGES=20 x PAGE_SIZE=25 (=500) to MAX_PAGES=200 x PAGE_SIZE=100 (=20,000) so a realistic already-tagged backlog fully drains in a single run (the window restarts at 0 each run and dedup skips already-created leads, so one run must reach the tail — 20k is generous headroom). Crucially the run no longer HIDES over-cap truncation: added `capHit` (set true when the last allowed page still reports hasMore) and return `cap_hit` in the JSON response; when capHit, a best-effort email_log row ('Page cap hit: swept N ...') is also written. A clean finish is cap_hit:false. ISSUE #2 (Apps Script getThreads per-label 500 cap): in setup/gmail-apps-script.gs added getAllThreadsForLabel(label) which loops label.getThreads(offset, 500) advancing offset until a short page, so labels with >500 threads are fully walked instead of silently truncated at 500. ISSUE #4 (per-page full re-enumeration): factored the combined de-duped ordered thread list into buildTaggedThreadIndex(), which caches the ordered thread-id list in ScriptCache for ~120s keyed 'tagged_index_v1' so a single cron run's page sequence (start=0,100,200,...) reuses one snapshot instead of re-enumerating the whole mailbox each page; falls back to re-enumeration if the id list exceeds ~95KB (ScriptCache 100KB limit) — correct, just slower for very large mailboxes. ISSUE #3 (email_log CHECK deploy order): the unmatched insert's error is no longer swallowed — captured into `emailLogError` and surfaced as `email_log_error` in the response (both the unmatched path and the cap-hit log). setup/GMAIL_TAG_SYNC_SETUP.md now documents running ADD_GMAIL_TAG_SYNC_CRON.sql BEFORE deploying the function as a hard, ordered prerequisite (step 2 before step 3). ISSUE #5 (created_by attribution): server already set created_by = profile.id (the matched owner); confirmed correct and kept. The client half (inbox.tsx) was changed to match (see FEAT-003 review_fixes). VERIFICATION LIMITATION: INTEGRATIONS_ONLY — no bun/deno/tsc; verified by inspection and brace/paren balance (edge function braces 90/90 parens 148/148; apps script braces 58/58 parens 178/178). Apps Script + edge function redeploy and the cron SQL remain out-of-sandbox owner steps.

Mirrors GMAIL_INBOX_SETUP.md tone/structure.

DEDUP/INSERT REASONING: The dedup key pair [realEmail, senderAddr] and the client_name/mobile/notes derivation are copied field-for-field from resolveLeadFields in src/routes/_authenticated/inbox.tsx, so the cron and the manual 'Claim' button can never create duplicates of each other. The service-role client bypasses the leads_insert RLS (admin/sales/bd only), so the cron can insert freely. mobile uses '' (not null) and client_name always has a fallback, satisfying the leads NOT NULL columns; source is set to 'email' so these rows dedup against and appear alongside the existing email-sourced leads.
